title: InviteMembersDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (dismissible = false keeps it open while sending) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTagInput, MonarchRolePicker, MonarchAppAccessPicker, MonarchTextField, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: invite people to a workspace by email address, with a role, the apps they get and an optional note, keeping any address the server refused with its reason.
whenToUse: From a workspace's members screen, when an admin invites one or more people by email.
whenNotToUse: To change the role of someone already in the workspace, use MonarchRolePicker on their member screen. To share one record with a person, use the share recipe.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = "Invite people", description = …, dismissible = !sending) { … }
MonarchTagInput(tags = emails, onTagsChange = { … }, label = "Email addresses", removeIcon = { … }, separators = setOf(',', ' ', ';'), maxCount = 50, normalize = { … }, validate = { tag, _ -> … })
MonarchRolePicker(roles = …, selected = role, onSelect = { role = it }, layout = MonarchRolePickerLayout.Compact, label = "Role")
MonarchAppAccessPicker(apps = …, value = apps, onValueChange = { apps = it }) // @ExperimentalMonarchApi, opted in at the call
MonarchTextField(value = note, onValueChange = { note = it }, label = "Personal note", helperText = "Optional", singleLine = false)
MonarchButton(text = if (emails.size > 1) "Send ${emails.size} invites" else "Send invite", onClick = …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = sending)

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles to choose from, least access first; the first enabled one is chosen when the sheet opens.

options.name: apps
options.description: The apps that can be granted; leave the picker out when the product has one app.

options.name: maxEmails
options.description: The most addresses per invitation, passed to MonarchTagInput's maxCount, as on the web.

options.name: validate
options.description: Checks each address before it becomes a chip; return a message to refuse it. Replace it to accept usernames.

options.name: allowMessage
options.description: Whether to show the personal note field.

options.name: failures
options.description: Addresses the server refused with the reason; they stay as chips and are listed in a danger notice.

states.name: editing
states.description: The addresses as chips, the role, the apps, the note and Send invite, which counts the addresses: "Send 3 invites".

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchTagInput refuses an address that is not one and says why; an empty list on Send shows "Add at least one email address."

states.name: sending
states.description: Send shows the loading state, every field is disabled, and the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: partly failed
states.description: The invited addresses are removed; the refused ones stay as chips and a danger MonarchInlineNotice lists each with its reason.

states.name: done
states.description: The sheet closes; the app shows a snackbar such as "Invited 3 people".

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: the title style, the tag input with its chips, the compact role picker, the app access picker, the multi-line text field and full-width primary and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's InviteMembersDialog is one component on Dialog. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchBottomSheet, because a phone dialog has no room for the chips, the role cards and the app list, and the sending state is a few lines of the app's state. The web's onInvite result ({ failed }) is the app's server response mapped to failures; the web's trigger prop is the app's own button; closeOnSuccess and the success announcement are the app's snackbar. The web adds a typed address on submit; MonarchTagInput adds an address when a separator is typed or on the keyboard's done action.
accessibility: MonarchTagInput reads each chip with its remove action and announces added, refused and removed addresses.
MonarchRolePicker reads each role as a radio button with its description; MonarchAppAccessPicker reads each app as a checkbox.
Send is read as loading while sending, and the sheet cannot be dismissed so the result is not lost.
The refused addresses are listed in words in a danger notice, not only by color.
Every button has a 48dp target; the fields grow at font scale 2.0 inside the scrolling sheet.
edgeCases: Check the addresses on the server as well; the email pattern only catches typos.
Duplicates are refused by MonarchTagInput; addresses are compared as typed, so lower-case them in normalize if the server does.
Pasting a list adds every address split by the separators, up to maxCount.
When every address fails, keep the sheet open with the reasons; when some fail, report the invited ones too.
